Members of Students Islamic Organisation (SIO) in Telangana were taken into preventive detention over their stance on Telangana government’s Israel-Telangana Strengthening Technology and Business Collaboration at T-Hub in Hyderabad | Photo Credit: SPECIAL ARRANGEMENT
Following the preventative detention of members of Students Islamic Organisation on Monday in Hyderabad , members of civil society accused the police of curtailing democratic right to question the Telangana government’s Israel-Telangana Strengthening Technology and Business Collaboration at T-Hub and called for divestment.
The civil society members said that the detentions were contrary to India’s consistent foreign policy of supporting Palestine. They pointed to what they described as a pattern of targeting educated and successful Muslim youth for raising questions on matters of public interest.
The Telangana police on Monday (November 16, 2026) picked up SIO members soon after civil society members had addressed the media raising serious concerns about the event at T-Hub.
Addressing the media in Hyderabad on Tuesday (November 17, 2026), academic Padmaja Shaw alleged a systematic pattern of targeting educated and successful Muslim youth. Referring to the detention of the SIO members, she said the action appeared intended to send a message that those who spoke out would face police action.
She recalled an earlier incident at the English and Foreign Languages University (EFLU), where female students were picked up over Palestinian literature. She said the police had reacted as though mentioning Palestine was a crime, despite the academic nature of the institution. Ms. Shaw also questioned whether Telangana Police were acting under the influence of the Union government rather than the State government.
While privacy rights activist Srinivas Kodali pointed out that Israeli investment was not new but the time has come to discuss and deliberate on divestment, S Q Masood said most surveillance systems were Israeli technology and efforts must be taken to challenge illegal surveillance in Telangana.
Khalida Parveen, another city-based activist said the students were picked up without prior notice and detained for nearly seven hours, until 6 am. She said there had been no protest call and questioned the police action against members of the SIO which she described as a national organisation working for education and employment without discrimination based on caste, creed or religion.
“They are not rowdy-sheeters or criminals. They were picked up from their office. This is a human rights violation,” said Ms. Parveen, comparing the situation under the Congress government to the crackdown on dissent in Uttar Pradesh.
Ms. Parveen said the activists had only questioned the collaboration with Israeli entities — some of which were involved in defence technology. “The only thing we said was not to allow defence technology of Israel in Hyderabad. T he Indian government has always supported Palestine ,” she said.
Sara Mathews, who had addressed the media on a previous occasion about the collaboration, said the police had also sought information about her movements following the press conference.
Professor Haragopal termed the detentions unethical and unbecoming of the Congress party, recalling India’s longstanding support for Palestine. He referred to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat’s visit to India, when then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi received him, and the honorary doctorate conferred on him by Osmania University. Mr. Haragopal also cited the c ommission led by Justice Muralidhar, which had documented Israeli atrocities before the United Nations.
Usman of the Association for Protection of Civil Rights (APCR) said the organisation had documented issues concerning tribals in northern Telangana, Christian missionaries and attacks on churches. He said the developments reminded him of the situation in West Bengal two years ago and demanded a thorough investigation into the detention of an activist from Ichoda at midnight.
“Detaining a person from Ichoda at 12 midnight is unacceptable. We demand that this incident be thoroughly investigated. Who ordered this? What is happening?” he asked, questioning the government’s claims of building a ‘Future City’ and a ‘Telangana Rising’ while, according to him, trampling upon the rights of the vulnerable.
